meta.note: Question-framing pathways. Not diagnostic algorithms and not substitutes for professional judgment.

pathways.components: Interview onset, settings, impairment; parent + teacher ADHD rating; school records; sleep/anxiety/trauma screen
pathways.nextStep: If discrepant, do not average informants; examine setting demands, observation opportunity, learning, anxiety, sleep, and relationships

pathways.components: Executive-function rating, academic screen, mood/anxiety/trauma measures, structured diagnostic interview
pathways.nextStep: Add direct observation or targeted learning/language assessment; obtain teacher narrative and work samples

pathways.decisionPoint: Complex profile, major academic impact, diagnostic uncertainty, or high-stakes eligibility?
pathways.nextStep: Refer for formal testing; ADHD diagnosis does not require cognitive testing in routine cases

pathways.components: Developmental history; current social communication and restricted/repetitive patterns; adaptive functioning; multi-setting collateral
pathways.decisionPoint: Lifelong pattern plus functional impact, not merely a low social-cognition score?
pathways.nextStep: Screen hearing/language, ADHD, anxiety, trauma, IDD; use social-cognition probes descriptively

pathways.components: Autism-specific caregiver/self ratings with cautious interpretation; pragmatic language; adaptive behavior; direct observation
pathways.decisionPoint: Does evidence converge across development, observation, and collateral?
pathways.nextStep: Ratings alone are insufficient; masking and psychiatric false positives need formulation

pathways.components: Comprehensive autism evaluation, cognitive/developmental and language testing as indicated
pathways.decisionPoint: Will formal diagnosis/eligibility materially affect care or services?
pathways.nextStep: Refer to trained evaluator; ADOS-2 is one component, not an oracle in a suitcase

pathways.components: Verify forms/time periods; interview both settings; impairment examples; classroom demands; school records/work samples; sleep/anxiety/learning
pathways.decisionPoint: Is there true setting-specific impairment, limited teacher observation, accommodation masking, or parent-child interaction effect?
pathways.nextStep: Do not require identical ratings; DSM requires symptoms/impairment across settings supported by clinical evidence

pathways.components: GAD-7 for many adolescents/adults; SCAS/RCADS/PROMIS form matched to child age and target
pathways.decisionPoint: Does the measure match anxiety domain and age, and is change interpretable?
pathways.nextStep: Pair scores with function, avoidance, risk, and treatment target; keep administration consistent

pathways.components: Developmental/educational history; curriculum exposure; work samples; timed vs untimed performance; anxiety/attention/EF; number sense and calculation probes
pathways.decisionPoint: What process is slow: fact retrieval, calculation, language, visuospatial organization, working memory, writing, or avoidance?
pathways.nextStep: Do not call it dyscalculia from speed alone; check instruction and functional impact

pathways.components: Standardized achievement plus targeted math processes; cognitive/language/attention/visual-motor testing only as hypotheses require
pathways.nextStep: School evaluation or psychologist referral; choose tests by process, not brand-name battery reflex

pathways.components: Safety and acute risk → developmental timeline → trauma exposure/symptoms → cross-setting attention/EF → lifelong social communication/RRB → adaptive/school function
pathways.decisionPoint: Which features predated trauma, are cue-linked, cross-situational, or developmentally persistent?
pathways.nextStep: Assess iteratively; comorbidity is common; avoid forcing one grand unifying label

pathways.components: One referral question; brief targeted measure; impairment questions; risk check; next-step collateral request
pathways.decisionPoint: Will this result change today’s decision?
pathways.nextStep: Choose one useful tool plus reasoning; postpone broad batteries

pathways.components: Therapists: screen, interview, observe, track symptoms/function. Formal evaluator: restricted performance tests, integrated cognitive/academic/adaptive diagnosis when trained
pathways.decisionPoint: Does the question require standardized administration, protected items, licensed scoring, or credentialed interpretation?
pathways.nextStep: Refer when scope/training/materials or high-stakes decisions exceed role; local policy and license govern
